_comment: Colour literals allowed to survive the reskin.
Matched by FILE + a distinctive CONTEXT substring from the same line + the LITERAL --
never by literal alone. '#fff' appears twenty times in this repo and only three of them are
QR quiet zones; a literal-only allowlist would wave the other seventeen through.
Context rather than line number, deliberately. An earlier version matched line numbers and
went stale the first time anything was inserted above an entry -- the census reported three
stale entries after a single unrelated edit. A substring survives the file moving around it,
and is still specific enough to name one element.
An entry whose context is no longer found anywhere is REPORTED as stale, not ignored: a
drifted allowlist is how a forbidden colour walks back in unnoticed.

chart.min.js.why: vendored Chart.js v4.5.1 -- never edited by hand

site/**.why: the marketing site is the SOURCE of this palette, not a target

worker/**.why: Cloudflare Worker, deployed separately, cannot link tokens.css

tokens.css.why: THE PALETTE ITSELF. Every literal in this file is a token DEFINITION, not a use of one -- auditing it is like auditing a dictionary for words. What guards it instead is the byte-identical assertion against site/styles.css and the mirror assertion against theme.js.

theme.js.why: The JS mirror of tokens.css, which exists because canvas, Chart.js, globe.gl and Leaflet cannot resolve a custom property. Its literals are the same definitions written again for a context that has no var(). It is not unguarded: the 'no token is defined and never read' assertion treats a token as live only when its VALUE appears here, so this file drifting from tokens.css fails that check.

lines.why: Google brand mark -- trademark. The sign-in button is required to look like Google's. Two verbatim copies of this SVG exist.

One gradient described by fourteen distinct alphas of platinum. The file states the case itself: tokenising them would mean fourteen tokens nothing else reads, which is the disease this migration cured.

Prose in a comment about the page base.
Prose. A comment recording the light-theme drift that this migration removed.

The one-page deal summary's PRINT stylesheet. Browsers do not print backgrounds, so a page whose colours are all near-white tokens comes out white on white -- invisible on paper while looking correct on screen. Print needs real black on real white, which is the one place in this app a literal is more honest than a token.
NOT A COLOUR. The placeholder text reads 'e.g. Payment for #123' -- an invoice number that the census's hex pattern cannot tell from a three-digit colour.
Prose. A comment explaining which colour was removed and why.

A paper document, like the portal's statement. These are read and printed rather than used, so they are light on purpose -- the dark palette would cost a reader ink and legibility. The text on them is tokens; only the paper is a literal.

Fully transparent. A compositing operand rather than a colour -- the globe is drawn on the page's own background, and naming this a token would imply it has a hue.
Prose. The comment records the drift that made tokens.css the single source of the palette, and naming the two values that disagreed is the whole point of writing it down.
